subject: SDG Weekly Compass - Week of 2026-11-02
overview_zh: COP31与COP17都在把气候与自然目标转成可谈、可核、可融资的制度安排。

items.title_en: Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit
items.summary_zh: Carbon Brief汇总约100份文件，梳理澳大利亚与土耳其共同主持下COP31上各国对气候融资、公正转型、减缓适应和全球盘点的立场分歧，显示谈判焦点已从笼统雄心转向机制边界、资金条件与议题打包。

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

items.core_argument_zh: Carbon Brief汇总约100份文件，梳理澳大利亚与土耳其共同主持下COP31上各国对气候融资、公正转型、减缓适应和全球盘点的立场分歧，显示谈判焦点已从笼统雄心转向机制边界、资金条件与议题打包。
items.core_argument_en: Carbon Brief compiles around 100 documents to map how parties at COP31, under the Australia-Turkey joint presidency, line up on climate finance, just transition, mitigation, adaptation and the global stocktake, showing that the real contest has shifted from broad ambition to mechanism boundaries, financing conditions and issue linkage.
items.why_now_zh: 安塔利亚会议将很快开幕，而战争、能源危机与极端气候同时抬高了各方对融资和执行机制的期待。它直接回应了COP30之后“实施COP”能否兑现的检验。
items.why_now_en: The Antalya conference is about to open, while war, an energy crisis and climate extremes are raising pressure for finance and implementation. It directly tests whether the post-COP30 promise of an “implementation COP” can be made real.
items.agenda_position_zh: 这是COP31正式谈判的议题分布图，也是各方围绕公正转型机制、气候融资和行动议程进行前置定位的文本基础。
items.agenda_position_en: This is the agenda map for COP31 formal negotiations and the baseline text for positioning around the just transition mechanism, climate finance and the action agenda.

items.title_en: COP17: Key outcomes agreed at the UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan
items.summary_zh: Carbon Brief指出，COP17完成了对2030年自然目标的首次全球审议，但“深表关切”的结论说明23项目标大多仍未进入可兑现轨道，资金缺口、捐助国范围争议与几近空转的基金暴露出现行生物多样性治理对融资、监测和责任分配的制度性不足。

items.why_now_en: This is the midpoint review of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, with just over four years left to 2030. Countries have signed the key texts, but the implementation gap has been put squarely on the table.

readings.title: Challenges of the OECD’s Tax Governance Regime Leading to the United Nations’ ‘(Re)entry’ into International Tax Law Governance
readings.note_zh: 文章指出，OECD主导的GloBE规则虽扩大了包容性框架，但其规则制定与治理结构仍偏向成员国利益，因而对发展中国家并不充分有利；作者据此主张联合国以更包容的制度程序重返国际税收治理，并建立UN层面的高层政治论坛以承接全球税收协调。
readings.note_en: The article argues that although the OECD-led GloBE rules created an inclusive framework, the governance and rule-making process still favors member states, making the arrangement insufficiently beneficial for developing countries; it therefore proposes a stronger UN role in international tax governance and a UN High-level Political Forum on International Taxation.
readings.journal: Global Governance: A Review of Multilateralism and International Organizations
readings.methodology_zh: 作者以制度分析为主，比较OECD治理安排与联合国框架下的制度包容性和规则分配效果；可得摘要未说明具体定量方法。
readings.method_en: The article uses institutional analysis to compare the inclusiveness and distributive effects of OECD governance arrangements with those under the UN; the available abstract does not specify a quantitative method.
readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期Carbon Brief关于COP31谈判中气候融资与公正转型争议的报道一起阅读，理解多边规则如何在程序包容性上遭遇类似争论。
readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside Carbon Brief’s COP31 coverage to see how multilateral rule-making faces similar disputes over procedural inclusion in climate finance and just transition.

research_directions.question_zh: 税收治理为何回到联合国？
research_directions.question_en: Why is tax governance returning to the UN?

research_directions.question_zh: 包容性如何影响规则分配？
research_directions.question_en: How does inclusiveness shape rule allocation?

readings.abstract_en: Abstract The Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) rules were created by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) to address the tax challenges arising from the digitalization of the economy and ensure that large multinational enterprises pay a minimum level of tax on the income arising in each jurisdiction where they operate. The GloBE rules have been viewed as a success in being able to establish the Inclusive Framework to get over 145 countries and jurisdictions involved in this international tax initiative. However, cooperation in achieving GloBE is not in itself proof that the rules are beneficial for all of the cooperating countries, especially developing countries. Developing countries continue to express discontent with the highly publicized cooperation accord of the Inclusive Framework. This article highlights how GloBE is not an overall resounding success of international tax law cooperation because the GloBE governance and rule-making process favors OECD member countries. Part 2 of this article discusses how the OECD being the governing organization naturally favors its member countries. Part 3 of this article describes the international tax law cooperation developments that have gained support at the United Nations ( UN ) due to the GloBE governance and rule-making process not being fully beneficial to developing countries. The article concludes with an analysis of why the UN can serve as a more suitable venue for international tax law cooperation because of its inclusive governance structure and processes. This article proposes the creation of a political tax forum at the UN —called the UN High-level Political Forum on International Taxation—as a key policy solution for the United Nations Tax Committee to implement.

readings.title: National Institutions and Global Public Goods: Are Democracies More Cooperative in Climate Change Policy?
readings.note_zh: 文章检验民主制度是否更能提供全球公共品，发现民主国家的气候政策承诺水平较高，但排放结果并不稳定；这说明国内制度可以提高政策输出，却未必克服搭便车、时间折现和运输部门等领域的结构性约束。
readings.note_en: The article tests whether democracies provide more global public goods and finds that democratic states make stronger climate policy commitments, but emissions outcomes are not consistently better; domestic institutions can raise policy output without necessarily overcoming free-riding, discounting and sectoral constraints such as transport.
readings.methodology_zh: 作者使用185个国家1990—2004年的横截面数据，比较民主程度与气候政策承诺及排放结果之间的关系。
readings.method_en: The authors use cross-sectional data for 185 countries from 1990 to 2004 to compare democracy levels with climate policy commitments and emissions outcomes.
readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期E3G关于英国预算与电力市场改革的研究动向并读，因为后者同样在处理政策承诺与实际减排/降价结果之间的落差。
readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside this week’s E3G item on the UK budget and electricity-market reform, which also grapples with the gap between policy commitments and real-world emissions or price outcomes.

research_directions.question_zh: 国内制度何时转化为减排？
research_directions.question_en: When do domestic institutions translate into emissions cuts?
Why do commitments and outcomes diverge?

readings.abstract_en: Abstract This article examines whether democracies contribute more to the provision of global public goods. It thus contributes to the debate on the effects of domestic institutions on international cooperation. The focus is on human-induced climate change, in Stern's words “the biggest market failure the world has ever seen.” 1 Using new data on climate change cooperation we study a cross-section of 185 countries in 1990–2004. The results show that the effect of democracy on levels of political commitment to climate change mitigation (policy output) is positive. In contrast, the effect on policy outcomes, measured in terms of emission levels and trends, is ambiguous. These results demonstrate that up until now the democracy effect has not been able to override countervailing forces that emanate from the free-rider problem, discounting of future benefits of climate change mitigation, and other factors that cut against efforts to reduce emissions. Even though democracies have had a slow start in moving from political and legal commitments (policy output) to emission reductions (policy outcomes), particularly in the transportation sector, we observe some encouraging signs. The main implication of our findings for research on international politics is that greater efforts should be made to study policy output and outcome side by side. This will help in identifying whether more democratic countries experience larger “words-deeds” gaps also in other policy areas, and whether there are systematic differences of this kind between domestic and international commitments and across different policy areas.

overview_en: COP31 and COP17 are turning climate and nature targets into negotiable, auditable, financeable institutions.
weekly_thread_zh: 本周共同议题是：多边目标已不再缺乏文本，而是进入分歧如何收束、资金如何到位、机制如何落地的阶段。
weekly_thread_en: This week’s shared question is how multilateral targets move from text into settled disagreements, actual finance, and workable institutions.

classic_readings.title: Challenges of the OECD’s Tax Governance Regime Leading to the United Nations’ ‘(Re)entry’ into International Tax Law Governance
classic_readings.note_zh: 文章指出，OECD主导的GloBE规则虽扩大了包容性框架，但其规则制定与治理结构仍偏向成员国利益，因而对发展中国家并不充分有利；作者据此主张联合国以更包容的制度程序重返国际税收治理，并建立UN层面的高层政治论坛以承接全球税收协调。
classic_readings.note_en: The article argues that although the OECD-led GloBE rules created an inclusive framework, the governance and rule-making process still favors member states, making the arrangement insufficiently beneficial for developing countries; it therefore proposes a stronger UN role in international tax governance and a UN High-level Political Forum on International Taxation.
classic_readings.journal: Global Governance: A Review of Multilateralism and International Organizations
classic_readings.methodology_zh: 作者以制度分析为主，比较OECD治理安排与联合国框架下的制度包容性和规则分配效果；可得摘要未说明具体定量方法。
classic_readings.method_en: The article uses institutional analysis to compare the inclusiveness and distributive effects of OECD governance arrangements with those under the UN; the available abstract does not specify a quantitative method.
classic_readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期Carbon Brief关于COP31谈判中气候融资与公正转型争议的报道一起阅读，理解多边规则如何在程序包容性上遭遇类似争论。
classic_readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside Carbon Brief’s COP31 coverage to see how multilateral rule-making faces similar disputes over procedural inclusion in climate finance and just transition.

research_directions.question_zh: 税收治理为何回到联合国？
research_directions.question_en: Why is tax governance returning to the UN?

research_directions.question_zh: 包容性如何影响规则分配？
research_directions.question_en: How does inclusiveness shape rule allocation?

classic_readings.abstract_en: Abstract The Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) rules were created by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) to address the tax challenges arising from the digitalization of the economy and ensure that large multinational enterprises pay a minimum level of tax on the income arising in each jurisdiction where they operate. The GloBE rules have been viewed as a success in being able to establish the Inclusive Framework to get over 145 countries and jurisdictions involved in this international tax initiative. However, cooperation in achieving GloBE is not in itself proof that the rules are beneficial for all of the cooperating countries, especially developing countries. Developing countries continue to express discontent with the highly publicized cooperation accord of the Inclusive Framework. This article highlights how GloBE is not an overall resounding success of international tax law cooperation because the GloBE governance and rule-making process favors OECD member countries. Part 2 of this article discusses how the OECD being the governing organization naturally favors its member countries. Part 3 of this article describes the international tax law cooperation developments that have gained support at the United Nations ( UN ) due to the GloBE governance and rule-making process not being fully beneficial to developing countries. The article concludes with an analysis of why the UN can serve as a more suitable venue for international tax law cooperation because of its inclusive governance structure and processes. This article proposes the creation of a political tax forum at the UN —called the UN High-level Political Forum on International Taxation—as a key policy solution for the United Nations Tax Committee to implement.

classic_readings.title: National Institutions and Global Public Goods: Are Democracies More Cooperative in Climate Change Policy?
classic_readings.note_zh: 文章检验民主制度是否更能提供全球公共品，发现民主国家的气候政策承诺水平较高，但排放结果并不稳定；这说明国内制度可以提高政策输出，却未必克服搭便车、时间折现和运输部门等领域的结构性约束。
classic_readings.note_en: The article tests whether democracies provide more global public goods and finds that democratic states make stronger climate policy commitments, but emissions outcomes are not consistently better; domestic institutions can raise policy output without necessarily overcoming free-riding, discounting and sectoral constraints such as transport.
classic_readings.methodology_zh: 作者使用185个国家1990—2004年的横截面数据，比较民主程度与气候政策承诺及排放结果之间的关系。
classic_readings.method_en: The authors use cross-sectional data for 185 countries from 1990 to 2004 to compare democracy levels with climate policy commitments and emissions outcomes.
classic_readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期E3G关于英国预算与电力市场改革的研究动向并读，因为后者同样在处理政策承诺与实际减排/降价结果之间的落差。
classic_readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside this week’s E3G item on the UK budget and electricity-market reform, which also grapples with the gap between policy commitments and real-world emissions or price outcomes.

research_directions.question_zh: 国内制度何时转化为减排？
research_directions.question_en: When do domestic institutions translate into emissions cuts?
Why do commitments and outcomes diverge?

classic_readings.abstract_en: Abstract This article examines whether democracies contribute more to the provision of global public goods. It thus contributes to the debate on the effects of domestic institutions on international cooperation. The focus is on human-induced climate change, in Stern's words “the biggest market failure the world has ever seen.” 1 Using new data on climate change cooperation we study a cross-section of 185 countries in 1990–2004. The results show that the effect of democracy on levels of political commitment to climate change mitigation (policy output) is positive. In contrast, the effect on policy outcomes, measured in terms of emission levels and trends, is ambiguous. These results demonstrate that up until now the democracy effect has not been able to override countervailing forces that emanate from the free-rider problem, discounting of future benefits of climate change mitigation, and other factors that cut against efforts to reduce emissions. Even though democracies have had a slow start in moving from political and legal commitments (policy output) to emission reductions (policy outcomes), particularly in the transportation sector, we observe some encouraging signs. The main implication of our findings for research on international politics is that greater efforts should be made to study policy output and outcome side by side. This will help in identifying whether more democratic countries experience larger “words-deeds” gaps also in other policy areas, and whether there are systematic differences of this kind between domestic and international commitments and across different policy areas.
